title: CFP: Northwest Archivists at 50
content:
NWA Annual Meeting 2027
Helena, Montana

May 19-21, 2027

The 2027 NWA Annual Meeting gives us an opportunity to gather, collaborate, and learn from the work of archivists and other cultural heritage professionals from around our region. Our 2027 meeting will be held at the Montana Heritage Center in Helena, Montana. Our theme is Northwest Archivists at 50 in recognition of the golden anniversary of our professional organization.

Anniversaries offer the opportunity to look toward the future of our profession by reflecting on our past. Our work stewarding the past teaches us that knowing where we have been informs where we are going. In celebrating this anniversary, NWA seeks to reflect on the past 50 years of archival work, highlight collections in our region, and envision where we want to go next.

title: CFP: Editing at a Crossroads, A Joint Conference on the State of Recovery and Documentary Editing in 2027
content: On June 25–27, 2027, the UVA Center for Digital Editing’s eLaboratories (eLabs) and the Association for Documentary Editing (ADE) will host a joint hybrid conference in Charlottesville, VA. Both organizations invite participation by documentary editors, recovery professionals, public historians, archivists, librarians, educators, students, digital humanists, community-based researchers, and all others involved in expanding access to documents from the past. We look forward to conversations about methodologies, technologies, formats, contents, audiences, and other facets of editing and recovery work. On June 24, eLabs will host in-person workshops on key topics in recovery and editing.

title: CFP: Postdigital Archives in Contemporary Literature: (Counter-)Practices and New Challenges in (Digital) Memory
content:
June 23, 2027
Goethe University, Frankfurt

Organization: Anna-Lena Eick (Vrije Universiteit Brussel), Johanna Vollmeyer (Universidad Complutense de Madrid) and Ulrike Mascher (Goethe-Universität Frankfurt) in cooperation with the Frankfurt Memory Studies Platform (FMSP)

Digital technologies have become so pervasive – or in Zara Dinnen’s words “banal” (cf. Dinnen 2018) – that they no longer register as distinct from non-digital aspects of everyday life. This condition, described as “postdigital” (Cramer 2014; Jandrić et al. 2018), is best understood as an interwoven set of cultural shifts that followed the “computerization and global digital networking of communication, technical infrastructures, markets and geopolitics” (cf. Cramer 2014: 13) and likewise affects the epistemic areas of memory and archives. Archives have always been active technologies of governance that produce epistemic order and social hierarchies (Stoler 2009). The postdigital condition raises new questions concerning the archive and memory that cannot be separated from questions of digital infrastructure and mediascape.

title: CFP: Faire parler les archives. Écritures de l’enquête familiale entre document et fiction. / Making the archives speak. Writings of family investigation between document and fiction.
content:
Faire parler les archives. Écritures de l’enquête familiale entre document et fiction. XVIe rendez-vous de la critique (Porto)
Porto, FLUP, ILC/APEF
APPEL À COMMUNICATIONS
Porto/Vila Nova de Gaia, 3-4 juin 2027

Depuis quelques années, la fiction narrative en langue française voit se multiplier des récits dans lesquels un objet (re)trouvé : photo(s), album-photo, correspondance épistolaire, carnet, archives, carte postale, maison, meuble, tiroir, objet, jouet, cadeau d’enfance, tatouage, etc., permet de déclencher une enquête sur la famille de l’écrivain(e) ou du / de la narrateur(trice).

En fait, ces récits se construisent bel et bien à partir du présent, mais sont motivés et interpelés par un manque, un silence, une faille qu’une trace matérielle vient interroger par le biais de l’enquête, cherchant par-là à restituer une histoire familiale incomplète et fragmentée, à recomposer un puzzle identitaire parcellaire.

title: CFP: Symposium of the 2027 FIAF Congress, “Times of Political Change: Film Heritage, Archiving and Agency”
content:
Symposium of the 2027 FIAF Congress
“Times of Political Change: Film Heritage, Archiving and Agency”
Monday 26 and Tuesday 27 April 2027
Deutsche Kinemathek, Berlin

In light of profound political upheavals around the world, the Symposium of the 2027 FIAF Congress in Berlin is dedicated to political changes in the context of film archives. What role does film heritage play in the collective memory of political upheavals? What impact does political change have on film heritage institutions? What can be learned from the past, what questions do archives face today, and how can they position themselves as resilient archives for the future? How have political changes been captured on film, and what has happened to these films once they entered the archive (and what if they did not)? This Symposium builds on the key reflections and proposals put forward in many previous FIAF Symposia, including those held in Bangkok in 2024 and in Rabat in April 2026. The goal is to provide a space for shared learning both within the FIAF community and in dialogue with all film heritage practitioners, scholars and institutions worldwide.

title: New Issue: Patrimoines, special issue on photography heritage
content:
Patrimoines 21 (2026)
« 200 ans de photographie / Patrimoine dans la rue »
“200 Years of Photography / Heritage in the Street”
(open access)

S’inscrivant parmi les célébrations du bicentenaire de l’invention de la photographie, ce numéro de la revue Patrimoines retrace l’histoire de la patrimonialisation de la photographie en France, au sein de laquelle l’INP a joué un rôle pionnier. Cette livraison s’intéresse par ailleurs aux problématiques de conservation-restauration et de médiation soulevées par les patrimoines exposés dans l’espace public (monuments historiques, œuvres contemporaines, peintures murales, art urbain, etc.).
